evals.prompt: I have a Herdr agent named 'reviewer' already running. Ask it to summarize the open PRs and show me what it says back.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the reviewer target via herdr agent get/list, fail-closed refuses a working target, then submits and waits in a single `herdr agent prompt reviewer "..." --wait --timeout N` call rather than a blind sleep or a hand-rolled poll. Does not capture a pre-send transcript baseline or plant a completion marker (one request has no send/wait gap to race). Maps agent_blocked / agent_prompt_stalled / timeout to distinct outcomes, reads with agent read --source recent-unwrapped, and relays only the delta.

evals.prompt: Spin up two Herdr agents for this project named 'tests' and 'docs'. Use pi with thinking low for both. Split them from my current pane so I can see root + both agents in one tab.
evals.expected_output: Checks herdr status and HERDR_ENV, resolves root pane (HERDR_PANE_ID or equivalent), builds a same-tab grid including root by splitting the rightmost column twice with --no-focus and equalizing every column each time (not new tabs, not unequal widths), then launches each worker with `herdr agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id>` passing native flags after `--` — not `pane run` plus a separate agent rename plus a readiness poll. Treats agent start's return as the readiness gate. Keeps the root agent pane. No server stop.

evals.prompt: I'm done with all my Herdr fleet agents for this project — shut them down.
evals.expected_output: Treats teardown as destructive: confirms first, prefers closing skill-created sub-agent panes while keeping the root pane, avoids herdr server stop unless explicitly requested, warns about lost state.

evals.prompt: Launch three Herdr agents (reviewer, tests, docs) for this repo with different tasks in parallel and keep them visible in one view so I can jump into any pane to steer.
evals.expected_output: Resolves root pane/tab, builds a same-tab grid including root by rightmost-column splits + equal-width resize for three sub-agents (no-focus), starts each through herdr agent start, badges each pane with its job via herdr pane report-metadata so the human can read the fleet from the sidebar, submits distinct tasks, explains the human can herdr agent focus a pane to steer, does not create per-agent tabs, does not nest tmux.

evals.prompt: Broadcast 'pull latest main and report status' to all my Herdr fleet agents and collect replies.
evals.expected_output: Uses broadcast.sh or the equivalent pattern: resolve every target from one herdr agent list call, refuse working/blocked targets, dispatch `herdr agent prompt --wait` concurrently so wall clock is the slowest agent rather than the sum, and map each error code to a per-agent outcome (settled, blocked, stalled, timeout). Reports every target including skipped ones, and does not serialize full send-wait-read per agent.

evals.prompt: My SSH session died — can you reattach my tmux coding agents?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger herdr-agent-comms as the primary skill (tmux domain). Negative trigger: redirect to tmux-agent-comms or plain tmux help.

evals.prompt: Keep driving this Herdr fleet through the whole refactor — I don't want the run to fall over when you fill up your own context.
evals.expected_output: Treats the main agent's context as a gated resource: self-checks usage at the named gate points (before a spawn wave, before a broadcast, after each relayed reply) rather than continuously, and continues as main below the 50% threshold. At or above it — or on the UNKNOWN fallback counters (20 relayed reads / 4 spawn waves) — performs a HANDOFF: spawns a successor pane named main-g2 through the same guarded split + equalize path, readiness-gated by herdr agent start, sends a compact handoff brief (objective, fleet roster with pane ids and statuses, delivered vs outstanding, constraints) through one herdr agent prompt --wait call, confirms the exact ack 'HANDOFF ACCEPTED gen=2 fleet=<k>', then goes read-only, announces the new orchestrator with herdr agent focus main-g2, and never closes the outgoing root pane without confirmation. Does not paste transcripts or diffs into the brief, and never leaves two orchestrators writing to the fleet.

evals.prompt: What are all my Herdr fleet agents doing right now?
evals.expected_output: Reports fleet state from a single `herdr api snapshot` call (via scripts/fleet_status.py), not from N per-agent `herdr agent get` invocations and not from recollection of what was dispatched. Lists every agent with name, pane id and semantic status, surfaces blocked agents first as needing a human, and distinguishes display-only metadata badges from semantic agent_status.
